# Welcome

This lab introduces **Tabular Foundation Models** in R using **tabpfn** and shows how to expose predictive models as tools using **ellmer**.

## Learning objectives

- Train a TabPFN regressor 
- Explore a "hot" dataset
- Wrap model workflow into a reusable R function
- Register those functions as LLM tools
- Build a simple AI assistant
- **bonus:** a dynamically created validation report *(no template)*

```{r}
# install.packages("pak")
# dev version contains R-only tabpfn & tabicl foundation models 
# pak::pak("tidymodels/brulee")

library(ellmer)
library(brulee)
library(rsample)
library(dplyr)
library(yardstick)
```


# Meet The Data 🏎️💨

```{r}
data <- datasets::mtcars

View(data)
```


# What is TabPFN?

TabPFN stands for **Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network**.

It belongs to a newer family of models called **Tabular Foundation Models**. Instead of extensive hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN performs inference using a foundation model trained over millions of synthetic learning tasks. It supports classification and regression on many small-to-medium tabular datasets with minimal configuration.

TabICL, another tabular foundation model, is also available in brulee. 

# Train a model

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

model_data <- data 

# our typical data split
data_split <- initial_split(model_data, prop = 0.8)
train_df <- training(data_split)
test_df  <- testing(data_split)

# x, y fit method
X_train <- select(train_df, -mpg)
y_train <- train_df$mpg

X_test <- select(test_df, -mpg)
y_test <- test_df$mpg
```

```{r}
# initial fit will download the pre-trained checkpoint, 
# fit doesn't actually "fit" a model, it is fast. 
# a convenient placeholder to stage the training data
# all time happens during the predict() stage

# fit <- brulee_tab_icl(X_train, y_train)
fit <- brulee_tab_pfn(X_train, y_train)
```


```{r}
pred <- predict(fit, X_test)

pred
```


# Introducing ellmer

ellmer provides a unified interface for LLM providers and supports tool calling from R.

```{r}
chat <- ellmer::chat("ollama/gemma4")

chat$chat("Hello! Please introduce yourself in one sentence.")
```


# Register the prediction tool

> **Note:** the chatbot provider & llm must be able to use 'tools' for this to work properly. 

tools need valid JSON types: type number, type string, i.e. pass a data.frame 'name' not a dataframe_df object.
```{r}

tabpfn_fit_and_predict <- \(train_df_name, test_df_name, target_var) {
  # Resolve string names to active global environment objects
  train_df <- get(train_df_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  test_df  <- get(test_df_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  
  X_train <- select(train_df, -all_of(target_var))
  y_train <- train_df[[target_var]]
  
  X_test  <- select(test_df, -all_of(target_var))
  
  #fit <- brulee_tab_icl(X_train, y_train)
   fit <- brulee_tab_pfn(X_train, y_train)
  predict(fit, X_test) |> dplyr::pull(.pred)
}

# Define the ellmer tool with string parameters
tabpfn_tool <- ellmer::tool(
  tabpfn_fit_and_predict,
  name = "tabpfn_fit_and_predict",
  description = "Fits a TabPFN model and predicts outcomes given in-memory R data frame object names.",
  arguments = list(
    train_df_name = ellmer::type_string("Name of the training data frame object in R memory (e.g. 'train_df')"),
    test_df_name  = ellmer::type_string("Name of the testing data frame object in R memory (e.g. 'test_df')"),
    target_var    = ellmer::type_string("Name of the target outcome column to predict (e.g. 'mpg')")
  )
)

#chat <- ellmer::chat("ollama/gemma4")
chat$register_tool(tabpfn_tool)

# Chat execution
chat$chat("I have 'train_df' and 'test_df' objects loaded. Fit a tabpfn model to predict 'mpg' and explain the prediction results to me.")
```

asking for the results so we can do some comparison on our end. *or register yardstick as a tool*
```{r}
estimated_vector <- chat$chat("
can you output the predictions as a single vector, 
like [1, 2, 3, 4]? 
do not include any words or backticks"
) |> jsonlite::fromJSON()

yardstick::rmse_vec(y_test, estimated_vector)
```

# Register a dynamic reporting tool 

```{r}
validation_report_fcn <- \(content){
 filename <- "validation_report"

  qmd_path <- paste0(filename, ".qmd")
  html_path <- paste0(filename, ".html")
  
  writeLines(content, qmd_path)
  quarto::quarto_render(qmd_path, output_format = "html", quiet = TRUE)
  browseURL(html_path)
  
  return(paste("Report rendered successfully and opened:", html_path))
}


validation_report_tool <- ellmer::tool(
    validation_report_fcn,
    name = "validation_report_tool",
  description = "creates a validation report for the user when they ask for one. please use this if they ask for a comparison between predictions and truth",
  arguments = list( content = ellmer::type_string("write a complete Quarto document content including YAML frontmatter, markdown text, and executable code chunks for tables or plots using R")
  )
)

chat$register_tool(validation_report_tool)

chat$chat(c("can you create a validation report? here is our ground truth: ", y_test))
```
